values: For arbitrary commuting invertible probability-preserving transformations S,T and complex f,g in L3, prove every r>2 pointwise variation and maximal bounds in L^(3/2), and almost-everywhere/L^(3/2) convergence of the symmetric sums H_N=sum_(0<|n|<=N) f(S^n x)g(T^n x)/n, H_0=0.

Bilinear ergodic Hilbert variation for commuting transformations as a consequence of annular triangular variation — Alec Kriebel (ORCID 0009-0001-9320-500X). Preprint date: 2026-10-06; production Zenodo publication verified 2026-10-07 UTC. Explicit fixed-positive-area cell restriction, summable signed kernel error and finite-window Calderon transference consequence of OpenAI's audited October 5 full annular variation theorem at commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. Includes maximal-tail convergence in L^(3/2); no r=2, noncommuting, one-sided Cesaro or broader-exponent claim, no first-priority or independent continuous breakthrough claim. Three distinct complete-package AI adversarial review cycles; earlier substantive package/scope issues repaired, fresh exact final package passed. Numerical support limited to kernel bookkeeping; extensive AI use, no conventional human peer review or full Lean verification. DOI resolves. Record: https://zenodo.org/records/23204591. Sources, audits and reproduction: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/tree/main/openai_followon_commuting_ergodic_hilbert

Sperner property for every standard graded Artinian complete intersection over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field: max over all ideals of the minimal generator count equals the maximal Hilbert-function value.

The Sperner property of standard graded Artinian complete intersections in characteristic zero. Alec Kriebel (ORCID 0009-0001-9320-500X); preprint/publication date 2026-10-06. Includes nonhomogeneous ideals, degree-one elimination and the empty/all-linear case; equality is attained by a power of the maximal ideal. Immediate corollary of OpenAI's Artinian EGH result and the known Harima–Wachi–Watanabe implication; no first-priority, Lefschetz, nongraded or unrestricted positive-characteristic claim. Two independent complete-package automated adversarial reviews completed; AI used extensively; not conventionally human-refereed at publication. PDF, source and verification: https://zenodo.org/records/23204810

Cubic hypersurface Kahler–Einstein/GIT compactifications for n>=5: identify the complex/polarized GH compactification and exact cubic Q-Gorenstein-smoothable K-polystable coarse space; classify ordinary metric GH boundary fibers.

Metric rigidity at the boundary of cubic compactifications — Alec Kriebel (ORCID 0009-0001-9320-500X). Preprint date 2026-10-06; production Zenodo publication verified 2026-10-07 UTC. Proves sharp singular Cartier-index rigidity for positive-dimensional projective klt weak KE Fanos with actual ample root -K=rL, r>dim(X)/2+1; stable tangent on quasi-etale covers and parallel complex structures +/-J. For cubic n-folds n>=5, ordinary metric GH compactification equals cubic GIT modulo conjugation, including all singular boundary points. Complex GH/GIT comparison is inherited and already public in stronger KSZZ form; attributed OpenAI upper-gap input, Li–Liu, Spotti–Sun transfer and DGP splitting. No first-solution/first-disclosure claim, scheme/stack upgrade, or cubic-fourfold counterexample. Two fresh distinct complete-package AI adversarial reviews of exact final v3 passed after minor supplement repairs; clean build and exact certificates reproduced. Extensive AI use; no conventional human peer review or full formal verification. Public downloads match reviewed bytes; DOI resolves. Record: https://zenodo.org/records/23204952. Sources/reviews/reproduction: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/tree/main/openai_followon_cubic_moduli

Uniform deterministic complete factorization, including multiplicities, over every explicitly represented finite field F_(p^m), and construction of irreducibles/extensions of prescribed dense degree without GRH, randomness or an integer-factorization oracle. Additional sparse target: all binary multiplicities with bit cost polynomial in term count, binary exponent length, field encoding and total degree of all distinct densely returned factors.

Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization — Alec Kriebel (ORCID 0009-0001-9320-500X). Preprint/publication date 2026-10-06; production Zenodo publication verified 2026-10-07 UTC. Dense factoring and prescribed-degree construction are inherited OpenAI family142/family029 consequences through Berlekamp, Shoup and Rai. Added sparse numerator/dense denominator descent has degree(V_k)<=kD, at most 2b dense calls of degree <=(b+1)D, b=max(1,ceil(log2(N+1))); arbitrary binary multiplicities and signed artifact cancellation. Construction degree d and optional fixed-root degree r are numeric parameters; no general poly(log d)/poly(log r) or practical-efficiency claim. Two distinct full-package AI adversarial reviews; portability and archival-pointer defects repaired, NEW exact-v5 review passed. Clean reproduction on Python3.11.8/3.14.6; public PDF/archive byte-identical to reviewed files; DOI resolves. Extensive AI use; no conventional human peer review, full Lean verification or first-priority claim. Full Gianni–Trager article inaccessible, bounded primary comparison recorded.
